summary: A 1970 note by Jon Postel and Steve Crocker saying a new protocol is coming. It prepares the group for the upcoming host-to-host protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 45 announces that a clean version of the Network protocol is being prepared for possible implementation. The authors also plan a meeting to explain unclear details and exchange comments and schedules.

subtitle: An announcement that a clean version of the Network protocol was being prepared.

tldr.problem: The network community was preparing a clean version of the Network protocol for implementation.
tldr.mechanism: The authors announce when they expect to send the specification and schedule a meeting to explain unclear details and exchange comments and schedules.
tldr.outcome: The one-page RFC is a notice of planned publication and discussion, not the protocol specification itself.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 45 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC is an announcement dated 14 April 1970 about planned protocol work.

sections.title: A Clean Protocol Document Is Planned
sections.content:
Jon Postel and Steve Crocker say they are preparing a clean version of the Network protocol, which they hope will be suitable for immediate implementation. They say they will send the specifications on April 28.

The note itself does not include the specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors are preparing a clearer version of the Network protocol and hope it will be ready to implement. This short announcement does not contain the protocol rules.

sections.title: A Meeting to Discuss the Details
sections.content:
The authors plan a discussion meeting in Atlantic City on Thursday, May 7, during the afternoon, one week after the Spring Joint Computer Conference. They intend to explain unclear details of the document and give participants time to exchange complaints, suggestions and schedules.

The note also says a network session chaired by Larry Roberts, with papers from BBN and others, is scheduled for Thursday morning.
sections.plainLanguage: The planned meeting will let participants ask about unclear parts of the specification and share feedback and schedules. The note also mentions a separate network session that morning.

sections.title: Scope of This RFC
sections.content: RFC 45 is an announcement of work in progress and a planned discussion. It gives expected dates and purposes but does not report whether the specification was sent or what the meeting decided.
sections.plainLanguage: The note states what the authors plan to do. It does not record whether those plans were carried out.
